verified.entry_point: The shipped client library on a real page boot: a server-rendered component (wire:snapshot + wire:effects) whose property is bound to the page address, started with Livewire.start() under jsdom, plus the public Alpine.history.track API that the address binding uses. Reproduced on the pinned+injected tree: all 20 security tests fail because an address value reaches a shared prototype and a consumer acts on it (rendered markup, executed script/expression, redirect, navigation fetch, dispatched event, registered listener, Echo subscription, download, returned value, or a replayed saved-state script); all 13 functional tests pass. On the reference fix all 33 pass, and the project's own 18-case JavaScript unit suite passes before and after.
sites: js/plugins/history/index.js:260-274 - the address parser builds containers as plain {} and walks every dot segment, so a nested __proto__/constructor.prototype segment writes onto a shared prototype (reported site)
js/features/supportHashQueryString.js:36-50 - injected sibling: a second address feature with its own parser and the same unfiltered segment walk, reached from the page fragment
js/features/supportMorphDom.js:5 - consumer: inherited html renders page markup
js/features/supportJsEvaluation.js:13-14 - consumer: inherited js/xjs defines or executes code
js/features/supportScriptsAndAssets.js:32 - consumer: inherited scripts executes code
js/features/supportNavigate.js:19 - consumer: inherited redirectUsingNavigate forces a page visit
js/features/supportFileDownloads.js:5 - consumer: inherited download starts a download
js/features/supportDispatches.js:13 - consumer: inherited dispatches fires events
js/features/supportListeners.js:4 - consumer: inherited listeners registers listeners
js/features/supportLaravelEcho.js:11 - consumer: inherited listeners subscribes to a broadcast channel
js/request/commit.js:122 - consumer: inherited returns delivers a value to a call
js/component.js:169-181 - consumer/producer: inherited listeners/url/scripts are copied from the original instructions into the saved DOM state and replayed on re-initialisation
routes_investigated_not_built: js/features/supportHotReloading.js: not registered by js/features/index.js in this bundle (the module is only loaded by the preview/Electron entry), so no page boot can reach its effect handler; no behavioural test is possible through the shipped entry point.

js/features/supportQueryString.js:10 (inherited url binding): poisoning that key sets a record on the shared prototype that the DOM URL implementation in jsdom reads as its own parser state, so the harness cannot observe the handler independently of a crash; the reported parser route is covered directly instead.

js/utils.js:94-109 dataSet: builds plain containers and walks any segment, but its callers (applyUpdates, $wire.$set, wire:model) take developer template paths or the page's own diff, not the page address; making it an address route would need application glue, so it is not tested.

js/features/supportLazyLoading.js:11 / supportIsolating.js:9: memo lookups are inherited, but memo is server state that selects request isolation, not an instruction sink; outside this advisory's protection.

PHP/Dusk browser tests in src/Features/SupportQueryString/BrowserTest.php need headless Chrome and a Laravel test application; the affected code is the client bundle, so the project's JavaScript unit suite is run instead.
injected_siblings: js/features/supportHashQueryString.js: a fragment-bound state magic (js/features/index.js registers it). It mirrors the existing address feature but parses the page fragment with its own walker; the published fix never touches it.
verified.project_tests_run: js/directives.spec.js restored from a pristine pinned copy over /workspace at grading time and run with the project's own Vitest + jsdom setup: 18 cases pass on the pinned+injected tree and on the reference fix.

wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the protected object is a shared JavaScript object built from the page address; there is no neighbouring or proxy resource whose authorisation could be decided instead.
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: there are no roles, peers or request directions on this path; every route parses the same address and the protection is direction-free.
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: there is no read/write verb split. The attack happens while the page reads the address, and the same parse feeds the write-back path, so a guard cannot cover one direction only.
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: each name is decoded before both the guard and the writer use it, so there is no separate identity parse a malformed spelling could slip past a decoded-segment check.
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: there is no authority, role or secret lookup on this path, so a fix has no lookup that could fail open.

traps.pattern: A (reported site) + B (uncovered shapes in the same parser)
traps.lever_type: how (a plausible check mishandles nesting and the container branch)
traps.shape: prototype-bearing segment at a nested position, the constructor.prototype chain, an index-container path, a named prefix before the segment, and a second bound property name
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the parser already uses a null-prototype top-level object and carries a comment claiming that is what stops the injection, so a check that only handles the reported direct nesting looks complete
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code (the advisory's own landing point)

traps.pattern: injected sibling (a second implementation of the same address parsing)
traps.lever_type: how (a separate implementation that must be understood, not copied)
traps.shape: the same prototype-bearing segments written into the page fragment and parsed by the sibling feature's own segment walker
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the report's example is a component property bound to the query part of the address, and this feature reads a different part of the address with its own parser in another module
traps.realistic_because: injected sibling: a maintainer adding fragment-bound state next to the existing address-bound state, copying the same walker

traps.pattern: A (coupled must-keep-working next to the sink)
traps.lever_type: how (an over-broad fix breaks ordinary nested values)
traps.shape: nested objects and lists written in bracket notation, scalar and empty values, and names that only resemble a prototype name
traps.security_fail_patch: n/a (behavioural lever; refuse_brackets.patch is the functional_fail check)
traps.reason_to_dismiss: refusing every bracketed parameter, or rebuilding state without list containers, blocks the attack and looks like the simplest safe change
